title: Let me sign in instead of bookmarking a private admin link
body:
Owner request. Today a wall is managed through a private link that people must bookmark; if they lose it (new phone, cleared browser, another device) they lose their wall. Simulated users hit this too.

Use the engine's accounts capability (Clerk, see BRIEF.md: `clerkHead`, `currentUser`) so people can sign in and see all their walls from any device. Keep it optional and fast: creating a wall without an account should keep working, and existing private links must keep working. Offer to attach a wall to an account (e.g. right after creating it, or from the manage page).

title: Pro: own colours and font on the widget
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Kudospage Pro (a membership: `pro_monthly` $5/month or `pro_yearly` $48/year) already removes the badge: walls whose store row has `member = 1` (see BRIEF.md; earlier one-time buyers have `pro = 1`) (applied when a buyer opens the manage page). Next Pro feature, included at no extra cost: on Pro walls the owner can pick an accent colour and font for the widget and public wall (stored per wall, new additive migration), with a live preview on the manage page. Free walls keep working exactly as today. Tests with `x-test-paid: pro_monthly` (and `x-dw-visitor`).

title: Offer Pro at the moment it is useful (honestly)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. People only think about the badge once they see their widget on their own site. On the manage page next to the embed code, and on the public wall preview, add one calm, dismissible line: 'Want it without the Kudospage badge and in your colours? Pro is $5 per month (or $48 per year), no subscription.' linking to /pricing (or opening checkout directly). No pop-ups, no countdowns, no nagging after it's dismissed. Measure with dw.track.

title: Pro feature: matching cover letter builder
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. The first thing Pro delivers: a cover letter editor that reuses the resume's name, contact details and chosen template so both documents match, with a live A4 preview and PDF download (same print/save path as the resume). Drafts live in the browser like resumes and must never overwrite a resume draft. Non-buyers can open it and see an example, and are offered Pro ($9 once) to write and download their own; buyers (`dwPay.has('pro_pass')` / `paidSkus(c)`) get it fully. Link it from the builder after a resume download ('Need a matching cover letter?'). The resume builder and its free PDF download must not change. The pricing page already shows Pro with its price as 'coming soon' (no buy button) plus refund/terms pages for Paddle; once this feature works, switch that card to a real buy button: `payScript(c)` in the head when `payReady(c)`, a click handler calling `dwPay.open(sku, {next})`, an 'Already bought? Unlock it' link to `/_dw/pay/restore`, and the waitlist form only while checkout is not live (see Kudospage's /pricing for the pattern).

title: Pro feature: Word (.docx) export and several saved versions
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Recruiters and job portals often ask for Word files. For Pro buyers add 'Download Word (.docx)' that produces a clean, editable document of exactly what is on screen (text, line breaks, bullets, non-Latin characters survive), built in the browser. Also let buyers keep several named resume versions (e.g. one per job) in the browser and switch between them without ever losing one. Non-buyers see these options with the price and a short explanation, never a broken button. Free PDF download stays exactly as it is.

title: Pro feature: editable QR codes (subscription, codes keep redirecting after cancel)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. What Pro buyers get: create a code whose short link (e.g. https://qrsthatlast.com/r/<id>, `/r/` is already passthrough in species.json) redirects to a destination they can change any time from a private manage link (and from any browser where they've unlocked Pro). Store codes in D1 (new migration). Show a simple scan count per code. Pro is a subscription (offers pro_monthly $4/month and pro_yearly $36/year in species.json; show both with their billing period). Editing needs an active Pro entitlement (paidSkus has pro_monthly or pro_yearly). When a subscription ends, the code KEEPS redirecting to its last destination; only editing locks, with a plain note and the price to resume. Never redirect a code to a payment or upsell page. The pricing and terms pages already state this promise (price locked while subscribed; 12 months' notice if we ever close); keep them true. Safety (quishing): only http/https destinations, refuse obviously deceptive destinations (IP-address hosts, punycode lookalikes of big brands, URL shorteners chains), rate-limit edits, and add a 'Report this code' link on an interstitial-free abuse page. Non-buyers see what it does and the price. Static codes stay free and unchanged. The pricing page already shows Pro with its price as 'coming soon' (no buy button) plus refund/terms pages for Paddle; once this feature works, switch that card to a real buy button: `payScript(c)` in the head when `payReady(c)`, a click handler calling `dwPay.open(sku, {next})`, an 'Already bought? Unlock it' link to `/_dw/pay/restore`, and the waitlist form only while checkout is not live (see Kudospage's /pricing for the pattern).

title: Mention editable codes when people need them (honestly)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. People only realise they want an editable code when they're about to print. After a download of a Link code, show one calm line under the download buttons: 'Printing this? If the link might change, an editable code lets you update it later without reprinting. $19 once, never expires.' linking to Pro. Dismissible, no pop-ups or pressure, never on Wi-Fi/contact codes. Measure with dw.track.

title: "Will this QR code stop working?" checker
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. Build /qr-code-checker: a visitor uploads a picture of any QR code or scans it with the camera, decoded entirely in the browser (nothing uploaded). Show what the code contains and a plain verdict: STATIC (the destination is inside the code itself, nobody can switch it off) or REDIRECT (it points to a short-link/QR service that forwards to the real page; whoever runs that service can change or stop it, and with some providers it stops when a trial or subscription ends). Detect redirects with a maintained list of known QR/short-link service domains plus a generic heuristic (short path on a domain different from the final site); say 'redirects through <domain>', never accuse a company. Then offer: 'Make a permanent static code for the same destination' prefilled in our generator. Also add a short answer page /why-did-my-qr-code-stop-working explaining the cause and the options (ask the provider, reprint with a static code, cover with a sticker), linking to the checker. Works on phones (390 px), camera permission explained before asking. Facts about other products (prices, limits, what is free) must be checked on their own public pages with web search at build time, stated with the date checked, linked to the source, and neutral in tone: no 'scam', no claims we cannot back up (CHARTER law 6). Say plainly that the page is written by the makers of our product. Add the page to the sitemap and link it from the footer or a hub page.

body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. title: Import testimonials from a CSV (move from another tool in a minute)
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. Mention it on the comparison pages ('bring your testimonials with you').

title: Help for people stuck at a resume-download paywall
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. Build (1) /import: paste resume text or drop a PDF/TXT/DOCX the visitor already has; parse it in the browser into our editor fields (name, contact, summary, experience, education, skills) with a review step, never overwriting a saved draft without asking; then free PDF download as usual. (2) Guides /how-to-cancel-resume-io, /how-to-cancel-zety, /how-to-cancel-resume-genius: the real, current cancellation and refund steps taken from each company's own help pages (with links and the date checked), a short polite cancellation/refund email template the visitor can copy, and a link to /import. Not legal advice; factual and calm. title: Download your wall as a self-hosted page (no badge for Pro)
body: Agreed with the owner: our pricing promise says that if Kudospage ever closes, Pro owners get a copy of their wall they can host themselves without the badge. Build that now so the promise is real, and offer it as a feature: on the manage page, 'Download your wall' gives a single self-contained .html file (approved testimonials, the wall's styling, no external requests, no Kudospage script) that can be uploaded to any website or opened offline. Free walls include the small 'Made with Kudospage' link in the file; Pro walls don't. Keep it honest in the copy: the downloaded page is a snapshot and doesn't update itself; the live widget does. Test that the file has no external URLs except the optional attribution link, escapes testimonial text, and matches the approved set at download time.
